value.name: Lucia accepts the news calmly
value.description: Lucia responds with a calm, non-angry silence and then says she understands what she has heard.
evidence: an angry silence. It was the silence of a person absorbing something she had half-expected.

value.name: Asha apologizes
value.description: Asha apologizes for what has been said or done, prompting Lucia to reject the apology.
evidence: "Do not be sorry. I would have been disappointed if you had said anything else."

value.name: Lucia reveals estate proposal
value.description: Lucia explains that he asked whether she would consider being bought out of her share of the house and staying for a year while he decides what to do with it.
evidence: "Yes. He asked me whether I would consider, if he bought out my share of the house at fair market value, staying in it for a year while he decided what he wanted to do with it."

value.name: Lucia postpones answering the proposal
value.description: Lucia says he is not asking for an immediate decision and is only testing whether she can receive the question in two weeks.
evidence: "He said he was not asking me to decide today."
"He said he was telling me he was considering asking me, and he wanted to know whether the question was one I would be willing to receive in two weeks."

value.name: Lucia answers the question carefully
value.description: Lucia tells him she is willing to receive the question later and will answer honestly based on what she knows then.
evidence: "I told him I would be willing to receive the question."

"I told him I had not yet decided what I wanted either, and that I would not pretend to have decided in order to give him an answer, and that if he asked me in two weeks I would tell him what I knew then and not before."

value.name: Asha praises Lucia's phrasing
value.description: Asha compliments Lucia on how well she handled the exchange and admits she borrowed his phrasing.
evidence: "It was your phrasing. I borrowed it."

value.name: Asha expresses estate gratitude
value.description: Asha asks whether it is improper to thank Lucia in an estate-client sense and then states her gratitude.
evidence: "Is it improper of me to tell you that I am — that I am grateful to you. In an estate sense. As a client. Is that a thing a client is permitted to say."
"Good. Then I am saying it. In an estate sense."

value.name: Lucia acknowledges gratitude
value.description: Lucia confirms that the gratitude is acceptable and formally receives it as part of the estate matter.
evidence: "That is a thing a client is permitted to say. Thank you."
"In an estate sense, received and noted."
